shared_elements: standing frontal anthropomorphic figure carved from a single stone block
head with brow/eyes indicated at top
arms bent with hands meeting across the chest/abdomen
incised low-relief lines on the head suggesting a cap or headdress
columnar, blocky body with squared shoulders
justification: Both are frontal, monolithic stone anthropomorphic figures organised in the same vertical sequence: a flat-topped head with incised cap-like lines, squared shoulders, arms bent so the hands meet over the torso, and a horizontal belt-like band below, with shallow incised detail rather than modelled volume. The clearest difference is proportion and density of decoration: A is a narrow, weathered pillar with sparse, eroded detail seen in situ, while B is a broad slab whose torso carries an elaborate array of discs and curvilinear incisions.
